question: Determine the coordinates of a point /(x, y)/ on the unit circle if you are given /θ = 30°/, where /θ/ is in standard position.

A circle has a radius of /7/ cm. If a central angle of /72°/ subtends an arc, what is the length of the arc? (Give your answer in terms of /π/)
Find the measure of the central angle in radians if an arc of length /8/ cm is subtended in a circle of radius /4/ cm.
solution: Arc length /(s) = rθ/ (/θ/ in radians). /8 = 4θ/ ⇒ /θ = 2/ radians.

The point \(P(-\sqrt{3}/2, -1/2)\) lies on the unit circle. Determine /θ/ in radians in the interval /(0, 2π)/.
Find the value of /cos(θ)/ if \(sin(θ) = 3/5\) and /θ/ is in Quadrant /II/.
solution: In Quadrant /II/, /cos(θ)/ is negative. \(sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1\) ⇒ \((3/5)² + cos²(θ) = 1\) ⇒ \(9/25 + cos²(θ) = 1\) ⇒ \(cos²(θ) = 16/25\) ⇒ \(cos(θ) = -4/5\).

question: If \(cos(θ) = -4/5\) and /θ/ is in Quadrant /III/, determine /sin(θ)/.
Explain why /cos(θ) = 2/ has no solution.
answer: /cos(θ)/ can only take values between /-1/ and /1/.
solution: The range of the cosine function is /[-1, 1]/. Since /2/ is outside this range, there is no solution.

question: Determine a positive coterminal angle in radians for \(-π/3\).
Find the principal angle /(0 ≤ θ < 2π)/ coterminal with \(19π/6\).

Determine the quadrant in which the terminal side of 100 degrees lies and state the coordinates of the corresponding point on the unit circle.
solution: /100°/ is in Quadrant /II/. The coordinates are /(cos(100°), sin(100°))/.

question: Express /1/ radian in degrees, rounded to the nearest tenth of a degree.
Find two coterminal angles of /70/ degrees: one positive and one negative.
Write the exact radian measure of an angle that is coterminal with 300 degrees but less than /0/.
Solve \(\sqrt{3}\) /cos(θ) + sin(θ) = 0/ for /0 ≤ θ < 2π/.
solution: Divide both sides by \(cos(θ): \sqrt{3} + tan(θ) = 0\) ⇒ \(tan(θ) = -\sqrt{3}\). \(tan(θ) = -\sqrt{3}\) at \(θ = 2π/3\), \(5π/3\).

A circle has a radius of /10/ cm. Find the arc length subtended by a central angle of /300/ degrees.
On a circle of radius /4/ m, an arc of length /2/ m is subtended. Determine the central angle in both radians and degrees.
solution: Arc length /= rθ/ ⇒ /2 = 4θ/ ⇒ /θ = 0.5/ radians. In degrees: \(θ = 0.5 × 180/π ≈ 28.6°\).

question: State the formula for arc length when /θ/ is given in degrees. Use it to find the arc length for radius /3/ m and central angle /45/ degrees.
A circle has a radius of /12/ m. An arc length of /6π/ m is subtended. Find the central angle in both radians and degrees.
solution: Arc length = rθ ⇒ /6π = 12θ/ ⇒ /θ = 0.5π/ radians. In degrees: /θ = 0.5π × 180/π = 90°/.

question: A Ferris wheel with radius /12/ m rotates through \(3/4\) of a full revolution. Find the arc length traveled by a point on the rim.

A point on the unit circle is \((-4/5, 3/5)\).
a. Determine /sin(θ)/, /cos(θ)/, and /tan(θ)/.
b. State the quadrant of /θ/.
c. Give one coterminal angle of /θ/ in /(-π, π]/.
solution:
a. \(sin(θ) = 3/5\), \(cos(θ) = -4/5\), \(tan(θ) = -3/4\).
b. Since /x < 0/, /y > 0/, /θ/ is in Quadrant /II/.
c. One coterminal angle in /(-π, π]/ is \(arccos(-4/5) ≈ 2.498\) radians.
